author: TEDx Talks
description:
What does true women’s safety look like in today’s world? Is it only about protection, or is it about creating spaces rooted in dignity, equality, accessibility, and inclusion?

In this powerful TEDx talk, Prof. Jaya Shrivastava explores the urgent need to rethink women’s safety at workplaces and in public spaces through the broader lens of social inclusion. She highlights how gender-sensitive policies, inclusive infrastructure, awareness, empathy, and collective responsibility can transform society into a safer and more equitable environment for all.

Through thought-provoking insights and real-world perspectives, this talk challenges conventional narratives and encourages individuals, institutions, and communities to move beyond symbolic safety measures toward meaningful systemic change.

Watch this inspiring session to understand why inclusion is not just a social value — it is the foundation of safety, empowerment, and progress.

Organized by: Mr. Lakhan Varshney

title: Reimagining Women’s Safety through the lens of Social Inclusion | Prof. Jaya Shrivastava | TEDxBBAU

Tamara Klink is a Brazilian explorer known for undertaking solo expeditions in extreme and remote environments, including spending eight months alone in Arctic conditions.  Lara Jeetley is a sixth-form student driven by curiosity and a love of learning. author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the very quality that makes a great educator or leader could also be their undoing? Through the stories of real leaders who shut down their empathy to survive and those who surrendered to it completely, this talk maps the hidden fault line between emotional wisdom and emotional paralysis. The most transformational leaders are not the most empathetic. They are the ones who know exactly when to feel deeply, when to step back, and when holding a boundary is not coldness but leadership. Drawing on real stories from educators and leaders across schools and institutions, this talk makes the case that empathy without self-awareness is a risk. Empathy wisdom is the capacity to connect fully with the people you lead while maintaining emotional clarity.  Dr. Michael Salvatore is Executive Vice President for Academic and Administrative Operations at Kean University, where he leads strategic initiatives focused on student success, innovation, data analytics, and institutional effectivenes
title: Empathy Wisdom: Knowing Your Emotional Limits as a Leader | Michael Salvatore | TEDxKean University

description: What if the greatest barrier to healing is not pain itself, but the way we misunderstand how others carry it? In “Why We Hurt Differently,” physical therapy professor, Dr. John Jonghyun Lee explores how pain is not expressed, interpreted, or responded to in the same way across cultures. While the body may register injury similarly, the meaning of suffering, the choice to hide or share it, and the expectation of care are shaped by culture. Through insights from healthcare, education, and everyday relationships, this talk invites audiences to rethink empathy beyond symptoms and assumptions. Listeners will leave with a deeper understanding of cultural competence as a practical tool for connection, and as a powerful act of love.  Dr. John Jonghyun Lee is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Physical Therapy at Kean University and a board-certified Orthopedic Clinical Specialist. He earned his Ph.D. in Science Education with a focus on healthcare education from Columbia University a
title: Why We Hurt Differently | John Jonghyun Lee | TEDxKean University

After surviving a drunk driving accident, Emeral was forced to rebuild physically, mentally, and emotionally. Through this journey, they examine the power of decision-making, the role of empathy, and how adversity can reshape perspective. At its core, the talk demonstrates that our most difficult experiences do not have to define us -in Emeral’s case, they became the foundation for growth, advocacy, and meaningful change. Elle explore ces moments où la technique atteint ses limites, et où l’essentiel se joue ailleurs.
Plutôt que d’opposer les approches, elle propose de les relier pour replacer la personne au centre, dans toutes ses dimensions. De cette réflexion émerge une boussole simple et universelle : les 4 Piliers de l’être, un repère pour traverser les périodes de doute, de fragilité ou de transformation.
